He began his career as a geophysicist on Macquarie Island. He later established Deep Ocean Expeditions and co-founded Space Adventures, taking commercial exploration from remote seas into the field of space tourism.

long_biography.plain_text:
While studying astronomy, Australian entrepreneur Mike McDowell supplied images from his deep-sea vent dives for a university astrobiology course. He began his master's studies at Swinburne in 2002 and continued computational astrophysics coursework while travelling. His interests linked environments rarely encountered by the public with questions explored in the classroom.

That connection also shaped the practical work of Deep Ocean Expeditions. McDowell arranged access to Russian MIR submersibles so paying participants could visit the Titanic alongside a scientific expedition. He later acquired his own submersibles, combining commercial diving with research and film logistics. Projects included support for a Japanese expedition to film giant squid and James Cameron's descent into the Mariana Trench.
